title: Implement session-memory compaction path
objective: Add the TS session-memory-first compaction path or an explicit compatible no-op when the required upstream session memory system is unavailable.
implementation_scope: Add session-memory compaction configuration with minTokens, minTextBlockMessages, and maxTokens defaults matching TS.
Implement capability gates/env gates equivalent to shouldUseSessionMemoryCompaction where Go has config support.
Load or receive pre-extracted session memory summary if the Go product has a session memory subsystem.
Calculate messagesToKeep index from last summarized message, minimum token/text requirements, max cap, compact boundary floor, and API invariants.
Build a CompactionResult using the session memory summary and preserved tail.
Reset last summarized message tracking after legacy compaction replaces history.
If upstream session memory extraction does not exist, provide an explicit TrySessionMemoryCompaction no-op with tests and TODO references so auto/manual compact call sites can be wired safely.
out_of_scope: Do not implement a full new memory extraction service unless a Go memory subsystem already exists.
Do not change the traditional LLM summary path.
acceptance_criteria: Auto and manual compact can call TrySessionMemoryCompaction first without nil behavior or cycles.
When session memory is available, the result preserves a bounded invariant-safe recent tail.
When unavailable, behavior is an explicit no-op and traditional compact continues.
Tests cover config thresholds, boundary floor, tool pair preservation, same assistant id preservation, and no-op mode.
risks: This task may reveal that Go lacks the upstream session memory subsystem; record that as a product gap rather than faking memory content.
Incorrect tail selection can produce invalid provider messages.
dispatch_prompt: Implement the Go session-memory compaction path, including TS-like tail selection and a safe explicit no-op if upstream session memory is not present.
